- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots after sharp upward spikes in history (e.g., after 70+ values), then corrects with a lagged downward drift.
- Underestimates in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, suggesting mean reversion toward lower levels after peaks.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth; fails to capture volatility or sudden drops in the last 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, especially when history includes recent high prices.
- Corrective adjustment: reduce forecast by 2–5% for the last 5–10 days if history shows recent peaks.
- If forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5 days, reduce by 10–15% to align with observed mean reversion.
- Lagged correction: if true outcome drops sharply after forecast peak, model should adjust downward by 5–10% in next 3–5 days.
